ogDesc: Chiang Mai is a genuine massage and spa town, running from foot-rub shops on the pavement to luxury spas you book a week ahead. blocks.html: Short answer: Want a polished spa with a welcome ritual and private rooms? Try Fah Lanna or Oasis Spa Lanna in the old town. On a budget but still want skilled hands, Lila Thai Massage employs formerly incarcerated women and charges a few hundred baht an hour. For a soak, an onsen and a full resort spa day, head to RarinJinda by the Ping River. Book ahead everywhere — slots fill fast.

items.name: Fah Lanna Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A day spa the whole city seems to rate, with a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice award every year. Three branches — old city, Night Bazaar and Nimman — all with a leafy Lanna feel, a welcome ritual and private rooms. Packages range from a single-hour Thai massage to a long half-day spa. Open 12:00 to 21:00; booking ahead gets a better rate and skips the wait.

items.name: Oasis Spa Lanna
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: The old-city branch of the Oasis chain, right next to Wat Phra Singh, built as Lanna-style pavilions in a garden — quiet and green despite the central location. It's known for the Lanna treatments that blend northern-Thai techniques with modern spa work, and offers free transfers within town. Pricier than a corner shop, but the setting and service earn it. Booking ahead is strongly advised.

items.name: Lila Thai Massage
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: Affordable massage with a genuinely good story behind it: it was founded by a former director of Chiang Mai Women's Prison to give released inmates honest work, and every therapist completes a 180-hour training course. There are 8 branches around the old town, open 10:00 to 22:00, with Thai and foot massage running just a few hundred baht an hour. Skilled hands, and your money helps people getting a fresh start.

items.name: Cheeva Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: An upmarket day spa near the northwest corner of the moat, holding around 4.7 on Tripadvisor from nearly 800 reviews. Treatment rooms are private villas, with a foot-washing welcome and refreshments afterwards. The Cheeva Experience package bundles a body scrub, wrap, Lanna massage, milk bath and a facial. It costs more than a standard shop, but plenty of guests say it's worth it. Book online ahead — it fills up.

items.name: Let's Relax Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: An easy-to-find chain with consistent quality — handy when you want somewhere clean and comfortable without gambling on what you'll get. In Chiang Mai it has branches at Pavilion Night Bazaar, on Tha Pae Road and in the One Nimman mall, open 10:00 to 22:00, which is longer than many. Foot, Thai and oil massage are all here, and the Dream package is a popular pick. Mid-range pricing, bookable online.

items.name: RarinJinda Wellness Spa Resort
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A riverside wellness resort in the Wat Ket area, good for a full spa day or an overnight stay. Its spa is billed as the most complete in the north, with a hydrotherapy pool, a Japanese-style onsen, steam rooms and singing-bowl sound therapy. You don't have to be a guest — day passes are available — and it's about a 10-minute walk from town. Book treatments ahead to get the time you want.

faq.q: Roughly how much does a massage in Chiang Mai cost?
faq.a: At a standard shop like Lila Thai Massage, a Thai or foot massage runs about 200 to 350 THB an hour. A mid-range day spa such as Let's Relax sits around 700 to 1,200 THB per treatment. Luxury spas like Fah Lanna, Oasis or Cheeva charge roughly 1,500 to 3,000 THB and up for a longer 2-to-3-hour package. These are rough 2026 ranges — check the actual menu when you book.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead, or can I just walk in?
faq.a: Most small massage shops take walk-ins, but the popular spas — Fah Lanna, Oasis and Cheeva — fill up often, especially in the evening and high season, so booking online ahead is safer and usually cheaper. Treatments at RarinJinda are worth reserving too, since slots and rooms are limited.

faq.q: How is Lanna massage different from regular Thai massage?
faq.a: Standard Thai massage focuses on pressure points and stretching, while Lanna massage is the northern style — it often uses a hot herbal compress, oils and a gentler rhythm. Chiang Mai spas like Oasis Spa Lanna, Fah Lanna and Cheeva feature this Lanna-style treatment as their signature, so if you want the regional version, ask for a menu item with 'Lanna' in the name.
